groups.ageBand: Tigers (Red): 11-12 years old, 5th grade / oldest kids
groups.name: Tigers

rooms.notes: Transform into a rainforest environment. Add a large visual waterfall installation along the side of the stage. Move all chairs to the back of the room for the week so there is open space for worship, dance, movement, and group engagement. Add clear age-group and animal-color signage so every group knows its morning and pickup meeting spot.
rooms.name: Sanctuary
MPR Room
rooms.notes: Hallway entrance should feel like passing beneath flowing water using hanging tinsel foil curtains. Cover walls in blue paper. Decorate with sea animals, coral reef elements, rocks, fishing nets, and lesson-connected props. Goal: calm, captivating room where kids dive deeper into who God is and how His Word applies to their lives.

rooms.name: Kitchen + Outside Kitchen Area
rooms.notes: Use the kitchen and outdoor area directly outside for snacks and lunch. Keep decor simple: paper-lined walls with vines, flowers, and leaves. Add a covering above the kitchen windows so it feels like a tropical hut or snack stand.

rooms.name: Pre-K Room
rooms.notes: Cover walls fully in gray paper to mimic a cave interior. Add rock and boulder elements made from cardboard and paper. Use this room for a quieter station, younger kid reset space, or themed activity rotation.

rooms.name: Tots Room
rooms.notes: Because the room already has animal wall paintings, keep added decor minimal. Add select wall or ceiling materials if needed. Use hanging vines, greenery, or ceiling elements for the Verse Vines theme.
Use as the 3-year-old hangout, potty-trained preschool support room, nap/reset room, or overflow space if group sizes require it.
rooms.name: Nursery Room
Elementary Area
rooms.notes: Cover all walls except cabinets and doors with paper. Decorate with vines, flowers, leaves, and optional animal cutouts. Wrap the two pillars in brown paper to look like trees, with chain-linked greenery extending upward as canopy. Arrange tables and chairs in rows for structured craft work.

rooms.name: Outside Area
rooms.notes: No major decorations needed outside. Keep all games and props on theme. Use relays, team challenges, water games if weather allows, and free-choice activities for Day 4.
rooms.purpose: Station 7, Games: Wild About God Games
Station 8, Volunteer briefing, supplies, or floaters
rooms.notes: Use for volunteer check-in, coordinator briefing, extra supplies, prep materials, or floater staging. Can also serve as a quiet problem-solving room during transitions.
rooms.name: Briefing Room

rooms.purpose: Day 4 face paint and quiet creative station
rooms.notes: Use washable, allergy-aware supplies, mirrors, wipes, water, and a simple design board. Keep line control clear. Offer a no-face-paint alternative.
rooms.name: Face Paint Room
BBQ / Fellowship Area
rooms.purpose: Family-style barbecue, lunch, parent connection, and pickup flow
rooms.notes: Use for setup, serving, seating, cleanup, and family welcome. Include allergy labels, trash cans, drink station, seating, and supervised games nearby.

pages.body:
Purpose:
Keep every station, room, decor plan, and low-cost backup option in one place.

Core Room Plan:
Sanctuary, Jungle Jam worship and dance. Rainforest environment, waterfall installation by stage, chairs moved to the back, animal/color group signs for morning gathering and pickup.

MPR Room, Bible Under the Waterfall. Hallway water effect with tinsel foil curtains, blue paper walls, sea animals, coral, rocks, fishing nets, and lesson-linked props.

Kitchen and outside kitchen area, Snack Shack. Simple hut feel with paper, vines, flowers, leaves, and a covering over the kitchen windows.

Pre-K Room, Cave Room. Gray paper walls, cardboard rocks and boulders, quieter younger-kid activity space.

Tots Room, Verse Vines. Minimal added decor because of existing animal walls. Add vines, greenery, or ceiling elements as needed.

Nursery Room, 3-year-old hangout or overflow. Use for potty-trained preschool support, reset space, or overflow.

Elementary Area, Creation Station. Paper-covered walls except cabinets and doors, vines, flowers, leaves, animal cutouts, tree pillars, and structured craft tables.

Outside Area, Wild About God Games. No major decorations. Keep games and props on theme.

Briefing Room. Volunteer check-in, supplies, floaters, and coordinator staging.

Budget Backup:
Use plastic tablecloths on walls when paper is too expensive or time-consuming. Focus the strongest decor in the highest-impact spaces.
pages.title: Room Design Blueprint

pages.body:
Purpose:
Day 4 is a freestyle celebration day. It should feel like the June fun day, with games, face paint, worship games, relaxed rotations, and a family-style barbecue.

Suggested Day 4 Flow:
9:00 AM, Fun Day kickoff in Sanctuary.
9:30 AM, Games and face paint open.
10:00 AM, Freestyle craft or memory keepsake station opens.
10:30 AM, Dance party / worship games in Sanctuary and BBQ setup begins.
11:00 AM, Family-style BBQ lunch begins.
11:30 AM, Open games continue for kids who finish eating.
12:30 PM, Closing celebration, family connection, prayer, and pickup.

Notes:
Pull games from VBS day 4 and day 5 options. Keep stations flexible. Use floaters to help with bathroom trips, line control, face paint, food setup, and transitions.
